explanation: When it moved to Amsterdam's town hall, it was trimmed on all sides to fit its new spot, losing figures on the left. Its nickname came later, from darkened varnish.

claims.text: In 1715 The Night Watch was trimmed on all sides so that it would fit a wall in Amsterdam's town hall.
Rembrandt painted The Night Watch, a group portrait of a civic militia company.
The Night Watch was not cut down to remove fire damage, to sell the pieces or to cut away mould.
The trimming of The Night Watch removed figures from its left side.
The name The Night Watch was given later, partly because darkened varnish made the scene look like night.
